title: Reader ingest: branch on InjectionSource for group log vs local-only
description:
Make the reader post pipeline write a group log entry only for peerable sources.

What: crates/reader/src/post/ipfs_write.rs (or wherever the group log entry is written after IPFS write)

Current flow (all articles):
  write to IPFS → write group log entry → update article_numbers + overview → 240 OK

New flow:
  write to IPFS → if source.is_peerable() { write group log entry } → update article_numbers + overview → 240 OK

Changes:
1. Thread InjectionSource through the post pipeline. Direct NNTP POST always passes NntpPost. NntpQueue drain passes the source from the envelope.
2. In the group log entry writer: skip entry when !source.is_peerable().
3. article_numbers and overview are always written regardless of source (local readers need to see all articles).
4. Group log entry for peerable sources gains an informational injection_source field (DAG-CBOR optional field alongside the existing verification_cid from stoa-f07d2b75):
   log_entry.injection_source = Some(source)   // informational; peers can filter if they want

Defensive rules:
- article_numbers and overview MUST be written for all sources including SmtpListId — local NNTP clients must be able to read list-injected articles.
- The 240 OK response is sent regardless of source — the SMTP caller does not need to know whether the article was peered.
- NntpPost source always writes the group log entry; no configuration can suppress it.
